minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Open Space Committee approved its November minutes and discussed ongoing work to revise its own bylaw: swapping an unfilled community-member seat for an Agricultural Commission representative, and possibly setting a lower fixed quorum in its charge as the master plan steering committee did. The chair reported plans to meet with the town manager, the select board chair and town counsel on these changes, gave brief updates from other boards, and the committee adjourned after a roll-call vote with no citizen comment and no budget items on the agenda.

what_happened.line: The committee continued advancing a bylaw change to replace an unfilled community-member seat with an Agricultural Commission representative.
The chair will ask town counsel whether the committee can set its own lower fixed quorum, as the master plan steering committee did.
The chair will push for the committee to be added to the town's notification process for Chapter 61 land transactions.
A member agreed to present on Riverfront areas to the Conservation Commission in January or February.
The committee approved its November minutes and adjourned by roll-call vote; no budget items or public comment were on the agenda.

why_it_matters: A lower fixed quorum would let this committee take official action with fewer members present, a procedural change town counsel has not yet weighed in on.
Swapping a community seat for an Agricultural Commission seat changes whose voice sits on open-space matters, including future land purchases.
Being added to Chapter 61 notifications would let the committee weigh in when farm or forest land under that tax program comes up for sale or use change.
